why: The v27 decision brief framed the ragged MUI mint as 'MUI declares no cell min-width, so its columns do not align'. That was wrong about the source. This is what the captured MUI Table actually renders.

rows.note: every row is EXACTLY the table root's width — rows fill, they do not hug

cells.note: each distinct width appears exactly three times — once per row. Every column has ONE width across all rows. The source's columns are ALIGNED.

whatThisChanges.previousFraming: MUI has no column model, so a ragged mint reflects the source.
whatThisChanges.correctedFraming: MUI's rendered table has perfectly aligned columns. The CSS table layout algorithm (table-layout: auto) computes one width per column across all rows. Our Figma mint produces two widths for the same column (127 and 159). The mint LOSES a property the source has.
whatThisChanges.consequence: This is a loss, and it currently carries no receipt. docs/32's bar is 'named or carried; zero silent losses'. A ragged mint of an aligned source is a SILENT LOSS — the exact class this project exists to refuse.

bearingOnGate1.question: does the table root hug its contents or fill its container?
bearingOnGate1.measuredFact: the captured root computes to 688px and every row computes to 688px — the rows fill the table and the table fills its container
bearingOnGate1.status: the fixture's hug-contents is NOT a source fact and is contradicted by the captured truth. Still an authoring decision to change, but no longer a coin flip.

bearingOnGate2.question: does table@1 gain a per-column width model, and where do the widths come from?
bearingOnGate2.measuredFact: the widths exist in the captured source: one per column, measured from the rendered table
bearingOnGate2.figmaPrimitive: Figma auto-layout has no column-aware algorithm. Each row is an independent flex row, so nothing computes a shared column width. CSS table-layout has no Figma primitive.
twoNamedLowerings: LOWER: compute one width per column from the rendered source and emit it as an explicit per-column width in Figma. Inputs are measured, not invented. This is the 'CSS->Figma gaps are decisions to author, with declared inverses' shape.
RECEIPT: declare table-layout:auto a no-figma-primitive loss and carry a receipt naming it, accepting that minted tables are ragged wherever content exceeds any declared minimum.
bearingOnGate2.notDecidedHere: Choosing between them is an authoring decision and belongs to the owner. What has changed is that it is now a choice between two grounded options rather than a request to invent a number.

firstPartyNote: There is no captured first-party ds.table under extract/computed/out, so the same measurement cannot be made for that source. first-party's mint aligns only because every cell binds minWidth 120 and all its fixture content is narrower.
